reason: POMDP adds an observation model Ω(o|s',a) and belief-state machinery to the MDP formalism for cases where state is not fully observed.
The POMDP belief update IS a Bayesian update over latent states — the form b'(s') ∝ Ω(o|s',a)·Σ T(s'|s,a)b(s) is Bayes' rule applied to the belief distribution.
Computing EVoI requires projecting future beliefs after observations, which uses the belief update equation iteratively.
VoPI is the upper bound on EVoI — the value if the observation were perfectly informative. Used to bound when no observation can be worth its cost.
Implicit belief is the LLM-agent's non-distributional approximation to the formal POMDP belief state — Markov-trivial but opaque.
Prior-encoding is the production pattern that makes Bayes operational in LLM prompts: priors live in the system prompt, likelihoods in tool descriptions.
Log-odds form is an equivalent re-formulation of Bayes that makes multi-evidence combination additive instead of multiplicative.
Calibration measures how Bayesian-coherent the agent's elicited confidences are against actual outcomes.
I(X;Y) is defined as the difference H(X) − H(X|Y) of entropies — built on top of the entropy primitive.
EIG of a tool equals the expected mutual information between the latent state and the tool's observation outcome.
Information-greedy prompting encodes EIG-optimal behaviour as a heuristic rule the LLM can follow without explicit EIG computation.
Both quantify 'distance' in distribution space but with different properties: MI is symmetric and additive across independent observations; KL is asymmetric and used for policy regularisation.
[CROSS-MODULE → M01] EVoI gives the formal basis for choosing dial settings — agents that don't account for EVoI tend toward dial 3 wandering rather than dial 2 efficiency.
[CROSS-MODULE → M01] EVoI is the principled foundation for ReAct loop termination — though the course doesn't introduce ReAct until 1.4, the formal motivation comes from 2.2.
Calibration is meaningful only for agents with elicited confidence — i.e., those maintaining implicit belief that we ask the model to quantify.
